answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each participant to lock a unique basalt-derived token that is only issued after a verified physical presence check in a remote tundra station. The check uses a hardware key that cannot be cloned, and any attempt to whisper the same attestation across multiple identities triggers automatic slashing of the bond. An attacker must physically visit the station for each identity, costing thousands in travel and time per fake account, making large-scale attacks prohibitively expensive.
